BiblicalUsage: The sense of rôʻîy is pastoral; as noun, a shepherd. In 1 Samuel 21:7, we read, "…certain man of the servants of Saul there…"; in Genesis 13:7, "…a strife between the herdmen of Abram's cattle…". You hear it again in Isaiah 38:12 — "…a shepherd's tent: I have cut off like…" — and in Zechariah 11:17, "…idol shepherd that leaveth the flock! the sword…".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word rôʻîy is in the Bible for a reason, and it carries weight far beyond its size in the text. I hold that rôʻîy still speaks, because the God who spoke then has not changed.
